title: Isaiah Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 8.

questions.question: What did the LORD instruct Isaiah to write about?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Isaiah to write concerning Mahershalalhashbaz as stated in Isaiah 8:1.

questions.question: Who were the faithful witnesses that recorded the events?
questions.explanation: Isaiah took Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah as faithful witnesses to record, as mentioned in Isaiah 8:2.

questions.question: What name did the LORD command Isaiah to call his son?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Isaiah to call his son Mahershalalhashbaz, as stated in Isaiah 8:3.

questions.question: What will happen before the child knows to cry for his parents?
options: The king of Assyria will be defeated
The wealth of Damascus and Samaria will be taken away
The waters of Shiloah will overflow
questions.correctAnswer: The wealth of Damascus and Samaria will be taken away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:4 states that before the child shall have knowledge to cry, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD spoke again to Isaiah after he recorded the name of his son.
questions.explanation: The LORD spoke again to Isaiah, as mentioned in Isaiah 8:5.

questions.question: What do the people refuse according to Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: The people are said to refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly, as stated in Isaiah 8:6.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8:7, who will come upon them like many waters?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Lord will bring up the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, as stated in Isaiah 8:7.

questions.question: What will happen when the king of Assyria passes through Judah?
options: He will overflow and go over
He will be stopped at the borders
questions.correctAnswer: He will overflow and go over
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:8 indicates that the king of Assyria shall overflow and go over in Judah.

questions.question: True or False: God is with us, according to Isaiah 8:10.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:10 states, 'for God is with us,' confirming that God is present.

questions.question: What should the people not say according to Isaiah 8:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:12 instructs not to say 'A confederacy' to all them whom this people shall say so.

questions.question: True or False: The name Mahershalalhashbaz means 'God is with us.'
questions.explanation: Mahershalalhashbaz actually has a different meaning related to speed and plunder, not 'God is with us.'

questions.question: What did Isaiah say he would do while waiting for the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah declares that he will wait upon the LORD who hides his face from the house of Jacob, as stated in Isaiah 8:17.

questions.question: What will happen to those who seek familiar spirits, according to Isaiah 8:20?
options: They will have no light in them
questions.correctAnswer: They will have no light in them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:20 states that if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of Jerusalem will be a sanctuary for the people.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 states that the LORD shall be for a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling, indicating it will not be a sanctuary for the people.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What name was given to the son born to the prophetess in Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: The name Mahershalalhashbaz was given to the son born to the prophetess as instructed by the LORD (Isaiah 8:3).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8:10, what will happen to the counsel taken by the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:10 states that their counsel will come to nought, emphasizing that without God, their plans are futile.

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 8:12, the people are encouraged to fear their confederacy.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:12 instructs not to fear the confederacy, indicating that fear should be directed towards God instead.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:13 instruct regarding the LORD of hosts?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states to sanctify the LORD of hosts and let Him be your fear and dread (Isaiah 8:13).

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Isaiah 8:15 regarding the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:15 warns that many among them shall stumble, fall, and be taken, indicating consequences for their actions.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 8:16 advises binding up the testimony and sealing the law among the disciples.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:16 instructs to bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples, emphasizing the importance of God's word.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 8:9 emphasize the futility of human plans?
options: By declaring God is with us
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring God is with us
questions.explanation: The declaration that God is with us in Isaiah 8:10 highlights that human plans without divine support are destined to fail.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:19 suggest about seeking guidance?
options: Seek the wisdom of the elders
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:19 questions why people would seek guidance from familiar spirits instead of seeking their God, emphasizing reliance on God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8:14, the LORD will be for a sanctuary and also what else?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 states that the LORD shall be a sanctuary but also a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to many.

questions.question: What is the primary instruction in Isaiah 8:11 regarding the way of the people?
options: To walk in the way of this people
To trust in their own understanding
questions.correctAnswer: To walk in the way of this people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:11 warns not to walk in the way of this people, indicating the need for faithfulness to God over societal norms.

questions.question: In Isaiah 8:22, what do the people look toward when they are troubled?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:22 describes that the people look to the earth and find trouble and darkness, indicating their despair without God.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 8:4 foretells that before the child knows his parents, Assyria will conquer Damascus and Samaria.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:4 predicts that before the child has knowledge to cry for his parents, the riches of Damascus and Samaria will be taken away.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 8:20 relate to the importance of God's word?
options: It is the light in darkness
It is only for the wise
questions.correctAnswer: It is the light in darkness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:20 emphasizes that if they do not speak according to God's word, it is because there is no light in them, highlighting the significance of His truth.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 8.

questions.question: What is the name given to Isaiah's son as commanded by the LORD?
questions.explanation: The LORD commanded Isaiah to call his son 'Mahershalalhashbaz' (Isaiah 8:3).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8:4, what will happen before Mahershalalhashbaz knows to cry for his parents?
options: The riches of Jerusalem will be taken
The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away
The king of Assyria will be defeated
questions.correctAnswer: The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:4 states that before the child has knowledge to cry, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be taken away.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the waters of Shiloah in Isaiah 8:6?
options: They are a source of life
They are a symbol of rebellion
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:6 mentions that the people refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly.

questions.question: In Isaiah 8:10, what assurance does the prophet give regarding counsel taken against them?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:10 declares that any counsel taken against them shall come to nought because God is with them.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:12 instruct the people not to say?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:12 instructs not to say 'A confederacy' to those whom the people shall say it.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD instructs Isaiah to sanctify the LORD of hosts and let Him be their fear.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:13 states that the people should sanctify the LORD of hosts and let Him be their fear.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:14 describe God as being for the houses of Israel?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 states that He shall be for a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8:19, whom should the people seek when they are in need?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:19 questions why a people should seek unto the dead when they should seek their God, who is living.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:20 say about those who do not speak according to God's word?
options: They have no light in them
questions.correctAnswer: They have no light in them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:20 indicates that if they do not speak according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 8:21 states that in their hunger, the people will curse their king and their God.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:21 confirms that when they are hungry, they will curse their king and God.

questions.question: What does the term 'Mahershalalhashbaz' signify in prophecy according to Isaiah 8:1?
questions.explanation: 'Mahershalalhashbaz' means 'speedy to the spoil, hasty to the prey,' corresponding to the imminent judgment and plunder by Assyria.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of seeking God rather than familiar spirits, as seen in Isaiah 8:19?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:10 emphasizes worshiping God alone, echoing the message of seeking God rather than familiar spirits in Isaiah 8:19.

questions.question: In Isaiah 8:18, what does Isaiah refer to himself and his children as?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:18 describes himself and his children as signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 8:14, describing God as both a sanctuary and a stone of stumbling?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 presents a paradox by describing God as both a sanctuary for believers and a stone of stumbling for others.

questions.question: What is the ultimate fate of the people as described in Isaiah 8:22?
options: They will be driven to darkness
questions.correctAnswer: They will be driven to darkness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:22 describes that the people will look unto the earth and behold trouble and darkness, and will be driven to darkness.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the name Mahershalalhashbaz signify in Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: The name Mahershalalhashbaz means 'swift to the spoil, speedy to the prey', indicating imminent judgment and the swift conquest of Assyria over Israel as foretold in Isaiah 8:3.

questions.question: What is indicated about the fate of Damascus and Samaria in Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:4 states that before the child Mahershalalhashbaz can cry for his parents, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be taken away before the king of Assyria, indicating their impending defeat.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 8, what does the LORD say about those who refuse the waters of Shiloah?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:6-7 indicates that because the people refuse the gentle waters of Shiloah, they will face the overwhelming flood of the king of Assyria, symbolizing destruction.

questions.question: What does God instruct Isaiah not to do in Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 8:11-12, God instructs Isaiah not to walk in the way of the people and not to say 'A confederacy' in response to their fears, highlighting the call to trust in God rather than alliances.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8 reveal about God’s presence with His people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 states that the LORD will be a sanctuary to those who fear Him, demonstrating His protective and nurturing presence amidst judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is highlighted in Isaiah 8:20 regarding guidance?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:20 emphasizes that true guidance must be aligned with God's law and testimony; if they do not speak according to this, there is no light in them, indicating the necessity of divine revelation.

questions.question: In Isaiah 8:9-10, what is the outcome of the people's conspiracies?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:9-10 declares that the conspiracies of the people will come to nothing and that they will be broken in pieces, reinforcing the futility of opposing God’s will.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in His warning to the people in Isaiah 8:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:13 emphasizes that the people should sanctify the LORD of hosts, reflecting His holiness and the call for His people to revere Him above all else.

questions.question: What dual role does the LORD play according to Isaiah 8:14?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:14 reveals that the LORD will be a sanctuary for those who believe but a stone of stumbling for those who reject Him, illustrating the duality of His nature in relation to faith.

questions.question: What is the significance of the children mentioned in Isaiah 8:18?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:18 states that the children whom the LORD has given are for signs and wonders in Israel, symbolizing the prophetic role Isaiah's family plays in God's plan.

questions.question: What warning is given in Isaiah 8:19 regarding seeking guidance?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:19 admonishes the people not to seek out familiar spirits and wizards, but rather to seek their God, highlighting the danger of turning to occult practices.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8:22 indicate about the state of the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:22 describes the people as looking unto the earth and seeing trouble, darkness, and anguish, indicating a state of despair and spiritual blindness.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 8 teach about the nature of God's judgment?
options: It is only for the wicked
It is based on human actions
questions.explanation: The chapter consistently portrays God's judgment as imminent and unavoidable, particularly through the prophecy of Assyria's invasion, as seen in Isaiah 8:4 and 8:7.

questions.question: How do Isaiah 8:6-7 and 8:11-12 synthesize to inform about faith in God amidst fear?
options: Trust in God rather than alliances
Ignore the needs of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God rather than alliances
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:6-7 illustrates the danger of rejecting God’s guidance in favor of earthly alliances, while 8:11-12 reinforces the call to trust in God instead of fearing conspiracies, highlighting the necessity of faith.

questions.question: What does the sceptic claim regarding seeking guidance from the dead in Isaiah 8?
questions.explanation: Sceptics claim that seeking guidance from the dead is acceptable, but Isaiah 8:19-20 teaches that such practices are condemned and that true guidance comes from God alone, reinforcing His authority.
